Next, junior Darren Thompson won the long jump on countback from Mark Faulkner of Team Solent. Jim Estall's silver in the 10000m moved us further ahead while Samson Oni equalled the winning high jump height and was unlucky to finish 3rd on countback.
Mary's Athletic Club members include Belgravians Darren Thompson, Nic Cooper and Hazel Mead. The lecturers are very approachable and are always willing to help.

Darren Thompson, who won the English Schools long jump championship, went on to represent Britain at the World Junior Championships at Annecy in France, where Chris Lambert also took part (in the sprint relay).

On the opening day Darren Thompson could only manage one legal long jump of 6.50 (+0.6) which left him a lowly 17th in his pool. Then a couple of days later Chris Lambert was involved in the sprint relay where the British team were disqualified.
With the non-arrival of John Regis our sprint squad included a long jumper (reserve Darren Thompson), a hurdler (Matt Douglas) and a 400m man (Dave Nolan).
In the long jump Julian Flynn just pipped Darren Thompson, while in the triple jump our only entry, Philips Idowu, almost made 16m off a short run-up.

Julian Flynn got the better of an injured Darren Thompson. In the high jump, junior Samson Oni leapt to 2.15 to prove that his English Schools win was not a fluke while Richard Aspden looked a lot lighter as he cleared 2.10.
